sentences.en: 250 years ago, the founding fathers gave rise to a new nation and an enduring myth.
sentences.zh: 250年前，开国元勋们缔造了一个崭新的国家和一个永恒的神话。

sentences.en: A myth about their virtue and what that meant about our virtue as a country.
sentences.zh: 一个关于他们美德的神话，以及这对我们作为国家的品德意味着什么。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, Jialin Yang, on the evolution of the founding myth, why we're still fighting about it, and why it may hold the key to America's future.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事嘉琳·杨将探讨建国神话的演变、我们为何仍在为此争论，以及它为何可能掌握着美国未来的钥匙。

sentences.en: It's Friday, July 3rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月3日，星期五。

sentences.en: Jialin, it is really lovely to have you on the show.
sentences.zh: 嘉琳，很高兴你能来到节目中。

sentences.en: It's great to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: You are massively overdue to be a guest on the show because for a very long time, you were unbookable as a guest on The Daily because you were the national editor.
sentences.zh: 你作为嘉宾来这个节目已经严重迟到了，因为在很长一段时间里，你作为《每日新闻》的嘉宾是无法预约的，因为你当时是国内新闻主编。

sentences.en: National editors don't really come on the show.
sentences.zh: 国内新闻主编通常不上这个节目。

sentences.en: They tell us which of their reporters can come on the show, and that was our relationship with you.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我们他们的哪位记者可以上节目，这曾经是我们和你的关系。

sentences.en: Could we please book this reporter?
sentences.zh: 我们能预约这位记者吗？

sentences.en: Yes, and I've been a huge fan, and it's just so lovely to finally be here.
sentences.zh: 是的，我一直是（节目的）超级粉丝，能最终来到这里真是太好了。

sentences.en: Well, now that you're not the national editor, you're a reporter focused on big ideas and big debates in the United States.
sentences.zh: 好吧，既然你不再担任国内新闻主编，你现在是一名专注于美国重大理念和重大辩论的记者。

sentences.en: And as a result, it feels very fitting that your debut appearance on the show comes on the anniversary of the United States turning 250 years old.
sentences.zh: 因此，你的节目首秀恰逢美国建国250周年纪念日，这感觉非常契合。

sentences.en: And on that anniversary, you set out to think about what the 250th really means, and you arrived at what I think is a really surprising answer.
sentences.zh: 在这个纪念日上，你着手思考250周年真正的含义，并得出了一个我认为非常令人惊讶的答案。

sentences.en: So talk about that.
sentences.zh: 那就谈谈这个吧。

sentences.en: You know, the 250th has been coming up for a while, and in these months leading up to it, it's honestly just struck me as kind of a weird time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，250周年纪念日已经临近一段时间了，在临近的这几个月里，老实说，我只是觉得这是一个有些诡异的时期。

sentences.en: Cruz dismantled plaques telling the stories of the nine enslaved people who lived in the president's house and were owned by President George Washington.
sentences.zh: 克鲁斯拆除了讲述总统府内九名被奴役者故事的牌匾，这些人曾是乔治·华盛顿总统的奴隶。

sentences.en: You know, leading up to this moment, you see this effort by Trump to really sanitize parts of our history.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在这一刻到来之前，你会看到特朗普试图真正美化和抹去我们历史中的某些部分。

sentences.en: any displays that might be seen as disparaging to America's paSt.
sentences.zh: 任何可能被视为对美国过去有贬低意味的展品。

sentences.en: He has had executive orders saying, you know, we can't mention slavery anymore from, you know, National Park historic monuments.
sentences.zh: 他曾发布行政命令说，你知道，我们不能再从国家公园历史古迹中提及奴隶制。

sentences.en: And at the same time, we're getting a lot more that's just about Trump in his own image.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我们看到了更多关于特朗普及其自身形象的内容。

sentences.en: Freedom at the White House on Donald Trump's birthday.
sentences.zh: 在唐纳德·特朗普生日那天在白宫举行自由庆典。

sentences.en: What an event.
sentences.zh: 多么盛大的活动。

sentences.en: And so you get examples like, you know, there's a UFC 250th match in front of the White House for his birthday.
sentences.zh: 所以你会看到这样的例子，比如，为了他的生日，白宫前有一场UFC 250周年的比赛。

sentences.en: You have him unveiling a commemorative special passport now, where it's a passport,
sentences.zh: 你看到他揭幕了一本纪念特制护照，在那里它是一本护照，

sentences.en: but also there's an image of him standing in front of the text of the Declaration of Independence itself with his signature at the bottom.
sentences.zh: 但同时也有一个他的形象，站在《独立宣言》正文文字的前方，底部带有他的签名。

sentences.en: So he's kind of inserting himself into the founding.
sentences.zh: 所以他有点把自身嵌入到了建国历史之中。

sentences.en: Hello, Washington, and a very big hello to America.
sentences.zh: 你好，华盛顿，向美国致以非常热烈的问候。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: And this just all is fully realized in the kickoff event itself for the entire 250th.
sentences.zh: 而这一切在整个250周年纪念活动的启动仪式上得到了充分的体现。

sentences.en: In 1776, our founding fathers met in Philadelphia and changed the world forever and ever.
sentences.zh: 在1776年，我们的开国元勋在费城会面，永远地改变了世界。

sentences.en: Trump basically does a campaign-style rally.
sentences.zh: 特朗普基本上搞了一场竞选风格的集会。

sentences.en: Just like those patriots of 1776 over the past 17 months, we have taken power back from the far-off political class.
sentences.zh: 就像1776年的那些爱国者一样，在过去的17个月里，我们从遥远的政治阶层手中夺回了权力。

sentences.en: And in this moment, he is just really fully claiming for himself and for the Republican Party, the founding.
sentences.zh: 在这个时刻，他真正且完全地为自己和共和党宣示了建国者的身份。

sentences.en: Together we stand on the shoulders of incomparable heroes such as George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, John Adams, Abraham Lincoln.
sentences.zh: 我们共同站在乔治·华盛顿、托马斯·杰斐逊、约翰·亚当斯、亚伯拉罕·林肯等无与伦比的英雄的肩膀上。

sentences.en: He's saying, we're the party that's going to protect the founding, all the mythology about the founders you love, about the country you love.
sentences.zh: 他在说，我们是那个将保护建国基业的政党，保护你们喜爱的关于开国元勋的所有神话，保护你们深爱的国家。

sentences.en: And in doing that, it's really kind of the apex in a way of something that's been happening for decades, where the GOP is just saying, this is ours.
sentences.zh: 通过这样做，这在某种程度上可以说是数十年来一直在发生的事情的顶峰，当时共和党人只是在说，这是我们的。

sentences.en: And we will make America great again.
sentences.zh: 我们将让美国再次伟大。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Happy birthday, America.
sentences.zh: 美国生日快乐。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, on the other side, on the left, you know, I feel like there's almost a kind of silence or awkwardness or just not quite knowing what to do or say in response.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在另一边，在左翼，你知道，我觉得几乎有一种沉默或尴尬，或者只是不知道在回应时该做什么或说什么。

sentences.en: Maybe just a little bit of, okay, you can just take it.
sentences.zh: 也许只是一点点的，好吧，你们拿去好了。

sentences.en: You know, this whole period, Jefferson and Washington were slaveholders.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在整个这段时期里，杰斐逊和华盛顿都是奴隶主。

sentences.en: There's so much to apologize for and to feel really bad about and guilty about.
sentences.zh: 有太多需要道歉的地方，有太多让人感觉非常糟糕和内疚的地方。

sentences.en: There's something just wrong with this era.
sentences.zh: 这个时代本身就有些不对劲。

sentences.en: And the more we learn, the more we feel like it's hard to feel proud of it.
sentences.zh: 我们了解得越多，就越觉得很难对它感到骄傲。

sentences.en: And so there's this kind of dynamic that I was perceiving.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时察觉到了这样一种动态。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I identify with what you're describing.
sentences.zh: 我对你所描述的深有同感。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: One side saying 250th is kind of ours to craft the celebration of.
sentences.zh: 一方说250周年基本上是属于我们来打造庆祝活动的。

sentences.en: The other side basically saying, good luck with that, because we don't know what to do with it.
sentences.zh: 另一方基本上说，祝你们好运，因为我们不知道该拿它怎么办。

sentences.en: You can take it.
sentences.zh: 你们拿去吧。

sentences.en: I'm oversimplifying.
sentences.zh: 我把情况过分简化了。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: That was the impression I was getting.
sentences.zh: 这就是我当时得到的印象。

sentences.en: So I wanted to explore, why does one side seem obsessed with myth-making, stripping away mentions of slavery at national parks,
sentences.zh: 所以我想要探讨，为什么一方似乎痴迷于制造神话、抹去国家公园中关于奴隶制的提及，

sentences.en: and the other side keeps being sort of caught up in the facts of it?
sentences.zh: 而另一方却总是纠缠于其中的事实？

sentences.en: And what is that dynamic?
sentences.zh: 这种动态究竟是什么？

sentences.en: And could we ever get out of it?
sentences.zh: 我们能摆脱这种状态吗？

sentences.en: You know, we are journalists, so we are, of course, obsessed with the knowing of facts.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们是记者，所以我们当然痴迷于了解事实。

sentences.en: We are not interested in myths.
sentences.zh: 我们对神话不感兴趣。

sentences.en: We are kind of in the business of anti-myths.
sentences.zh: 我们算是从事反神话行业的。

sentences.en: But the more you learn about the founding and how the country has thought about its founding, which is what I'm interested in, right,
sentences.zh: 但你对建国以及这个国家如何看待其建国了解得越多——这也是我感兴趣的，对吧——

sentences.en: what struck me is that actually throughout our history,
sentences.zh: 令我震惊的是，其实在我们的整个历史中，

sentences.en: basically from the very beginning after the founding, there has been a really important other history where people are making myths out of the founding.
sentences.zh: 基本上从建国刚开始的时候起，就存在着另一段非常重要的历史，人们在把建国过程神话化。

sentences.en: And the myths are not technically factual per se, but they're really powerful for people.
sentences.zh: 这些神话在严格意义上或许并非完全符合事实，但对人们来说它们具有强大的力量。

sentences.en: And what have you come to understand about why the myth of America's founding is so powerful and important?
sentences.zh: 关于为什么美国建国的神话如此强大和重要，你了解到了什么？

sentences.en: So I can see that this feels like very fraught to even say that let's talk about myths, because if you think about myths as lies, there is a lot of lying about history, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我能看出，仅仅说“让我们来谈谈神话”这件事就让人感到非常紧绷，因为如果你把神话等同于谎言，那历史中确实有很多谎言，对吧？

sentences.en: And we are living in a time of just constant political lying.
sentences.zh: 而我们正生活在一个充斥着持续政治谎言的时代。

sentences.en: But that's not really what I'm talking about when I talk about a myth.
sentences.zh: 但当我谈论神话时，指的并不是这个。

sentences.en: And when I talk to historians, they're pointing to an idea of myth as not about, you know, lying versus having facts, but about myths that are stories.
sentences.zh: 当我与历史学家交谈时，他们所指的神话概念，不是关于谎言与事实的对立，而是指作为故事的神话。

sentences.en: And these are ways that a group of people can figure out what they stand for, what their identity is, who they are.
sentences.zh: 这些是一群人用来弄清楚他们主张什么、他们的身份是什么、他们是谁的方式。

sentences.en: And historians I spoke with, even the ones who are just deep in the muck of here's what went wrong, here's where we've fallen short,
sentences.zh: 我交谈过的历史学家，甚至那些深入研究哪里出了问题、我们在哪里有所欠缺的历史学家，

sentences.en: you know, many of them argue that we can't abandon the effort to make myth out of the founding.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们中的许多人认为，我们不能放弃将建国历史神话化的努力。

sentences.en: That if we stop arguing about it and really having debates about it, we are essentially no longer in a way practicing the heart of democracy,
sentences.zh: 如果我们停止对它的争论、不再真正进行辩论，我们实质上就不再是在践行民主的核心，

sentences.en: which is to talk about what we're doing here, where we want the future to go, and to find those answers, Americans have over and over again gone to the founding.
sentences.zh: 民主的核心就是讨论我们在这里做什么、我们希望未来走向何方，而为了找到这些答案，美国人一次又一次地回溯建国历史。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is a very unexpected place for us to be.
sentences.zh: 是的，对我们来说，这是一个非常意想不到的境地。

sentences.en: Kind of like Today on the Daily, the case for the American mythology of our founding.
sentences.zh: 有点像今天的《每日新闻》：关于我们建国的美国神话的案例。

sentences.en: And I want to hear about the role of myth throughout the last 250 years.
sentences.zh: 我想听听神话在过去250年中发挥的作用。

sentences.en: But let's just start with the foundational myth.
sentences.zh: 但让我们先从奠基神话开始。

sentences.en: What exactly do we mean when we talk about the myth of America's founding?
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论美国建国的神话时，我们到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: What is the myth that we're really describing?
sentences.zh: 我们真正在描述的神话是什么？

sentences.en: I think we all in a way remember some version of this.
sentences.zh: 我想我们在某种程度上都记得某种版本的神话。

sentences.en: So it's the version where a handful of men get together and some would argue they're divinely touched by God even.
sentences.zh: 那就是这样一种版本：少数几个男人聚在一起，甚至有人会说他们受到了上帝的神圣触碰。

sentences.en: And they found this country and they write these documents and the documents themselves are almost divine and they sort of tell us what to do.
sentences.zh: 他们建立了这个国家，他们写下了这些文件，这些文件本身几乎是神圣的，它们在某种程度上告诉我们该怎么做。

sentences.en: And these are people who are just the height of virtue.
sentences.zh: 而这些人正是美德的巅峰。

sentences.en: And not only is this a country that is great, but it is like, you know, God has chosen this country to bring the kingdom.
sentences.zh: 这个国家不仅伟大，而且就像是，你知道的，上帝选择了这个国家来带来天国。

sentences.en: It's really, really lofty.
sentences.zh: 这真的是非常非常崇高。

sentences.en: And as that myth was emerging, what role was it serving in the early years of our country's history?
sentences.zh: 随着那个神话的浮现，它在我们国家历史的早期起到了什么作用？

sentences.en: I think for this country, we have to remember at the very beginning, it's a very unusual place to be founding a country.
sentences.zh: 我想对于这个国家，我们必须记住在最初的时候，在一个新建立的国家里，这是一个非常不同寻常的地方。

sentences.en: There's a couple of things that the country is missing that usually bind together a people, right?
sentences.zh: 这个国家缺少了几样通常能将一个民族凝聚在一起的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: There is no unique language.
sentences.zh: 这里没有独特的语言。

sentences.en: There is no official single religion.
sentences.zh: 这里没有官方的单一宗教。

sentences.en: You know, there's a bunch of different Christian groups jostling.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这里有一群不同的基督教派系在争夺影响力。

sentences.en: But there isn't one official, you know, governmentally chosen church.
sentences.zh: 但没有一个官方的、由政府选定的教会。

sentences.en: And the literal geographic borders of the country are just constantly in flux, to put it nicely.
sentences.zh: 委婉地说，这个国家的字面地理边界一直在不断变动。

sentences.en: And so you don't have the unusual things that you need to say, okay, we are one, right?
sentences.zh: 所以你并不具备那些用来宣告“好吧，我们是一个整体”的不寻常要素，对吧？

sentences.en: Here's our language.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的语言。

sentences.en: Here's our culture.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的文化。

sentences.en: And so this is why the founding, I think, becomes so important from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么我认为建国故事从一开始就变得如此重要。

sentences.en: What's going to keep this whole thing together?
sentences.zh: 究竟是什么要把这一切凝聚在一起？

sentences.en: We've revolted.
sentences.zh: 我们已经反叛了。

sentences.en: Now we're here.
sentences.zh: 现在我们在这里。

sentences.en: We need a story.
sentences.zh: 我们需要一个故事。

sentences.en: And during this time in the 19th century, 18th century, when the country's being founded and people are beginning to tell stories about it,
sentences.zh: 在19世纪、18世纪的这段时间里，当国家正在建立，人们开始讲述关于它的故事时，

sentences.en: anybody can just start writing stories about the paSt.
sentences.zh: 任何人都可以开始书写关于过去的故事。

sentences.en: So history at this time is different from maybe how we imagine it today or think about it today.
sentences.zh: 所以那时的历史可能与我们今天想象或看待它的方式有所不同。

sentences.en: It's a little bit more like literature.
sentences.zh: 它有点更像是文学。

sentences.en: So it's a set of great stories that people like to tell over and over.
sentences.zh: 所以它是一套人们喜欢一遍又一遍讲述的伟大故事。

sentences.en: Not just because they're great yarns.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是因为它们是精彩的传奇。

sentences.en: They give people a sense of meaning.
sentences.zh: 它们赋予了人们意义感。

sentences.en: They bring people together.
sentences.zh: 它们将人们凝聚在一起。

sentences.en: And that's going to be the history that sticks.
sentences.zh: 这将是流传下来的历史。

sentences.en: And to me, the very best example of this is a story that all of us know centuries later about George Washington.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，这最好的例子就是一个几个世纪后我们所有人都知道的关于乔治·华盛顿的故事。

sentences.en: So in 1800, right after George Washington dies, everyone's already thinking, oh, my gosh, our ultimate founder is gone.
sentences.zh: 所以在1800年，就在乔治·华盛顿去世后，每个人都在想，天哪，我们最伟大的创始人离去了。

sentences.en: It's time to show how much he was sort of the ultimate great American.
sentences.zh: 现在是时候展现他是如何成为终极伟大美国人的了。

sentences.en: And this traveling Bible salesman named Mason Locke Weems, who, again, is not, you know, there's no professional training for historians.
sentences.zh: 有个名叫梅森·洛克·威姆斯的巡回圣经推销员，再次说明，当时并没有历史学家的专业培训。

sentences.en: He's a guy who loves George Washington.
sentences.zh: 他是一个热爱乔治·华盛顿的人。

sentences.en: And he writes what he calls is a biography of Washington.
sentences.zh: 他写了一本他称之为华盛顿传记的书。

sentences.en: And it's filled with stories like the famous story of Washington chopping down a cherry tree when he's a child.
sentences.zh: 里面充满了各种故事，比如著名的华盛顿小时候砍倒樱桃树的故事。

sentences.en: We all know the story, right?
sentences.zh: 我们都知道这个故事，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He's a young boy.
sentences.zh: 他是个小男孩。

sentences.en: He's chopping down a cherry tree.
sentences.zh: 他在砍一棵樱桃树。

sentences.en: And later he admits to his father, father, I could not tell a lie.
sentences.zh: 后来他向父亲坦白：父亲，我不能说谎。

sentences.en: And the story is utterly false.
sentences.zh: 而这个故事完全是虚构的。

sentences.en: There is no evidence that it ever happened.
sentences.zh: 没有任何证据证明它曾发生过。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And by the way, no kid would ever chop down a cherry tree and then confess it.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，没有哪个孩子会砍倒一棵樱桃树然后主动承认。

sentences.en: But George Washington is so pure, so virtuous, according to this myth, that he was incapable of committing the totally understandable childhood act of lying to his parents.
sentences.zh: 但根据这个神话，乔治·华盛顿是如此纯洁、如此有美德，以至于他无法做出对父母撒谎这种完全可以理解的童年举动。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this whole book, this purported biography, turns Washington into like a model for children, right?
sentences.zh: 整本书，也就是这本所谓的传记，把华盛顿塑造成了一个儿童的楷模，对吧？

sentences.en: It's like he's the star of these fairy tales so that you can teach children what it means to be a good person, right?
sentences.zh: 就好像他是这些童话故事的主角，这样你就可以教导孩子们做一个好人意味着什么，对吧？

sentences.en: What it means to have a great character like your great national leader, George Washington.
sentences.zh: 拥有伟大的品格意味着什么，就像你们伟大的国家领袖乔治·华盛顿一样。

sentences.en: And so that is right out of the gate at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切在一开始就已经注定了。

sentences.en: And other stories are told about the founders, all of them making them seem like these total models of virtuous American citizenship.
sentences.zh: 关于国父们还有其他的故事，所有这些故事都让他们看起来像是具有美德的美国公民的完美楷模。

sentences.en: I'm curious, as these myths are making their way across America, you know, in school books, at kitchen tables, how widely shared do you think that these myths are becoming?
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，随着这些神话在全美流传，比如在课本里、在餐桌上，你认为这些神话的普及程度有多高？

sentences.en: I think the mythology that America is a really special country and unlike anything anyone has ever seen before is really taking hold across many Americans.
sentences.zh: 我认为“美国是一个真正特别的国家，不同于以往任何人见过的任何事物”这种神话，确实在许多美国人心中扎根了。

sentences.en: Which is not to say that it is a perfect country because people immediately look at all men are created equal in the Declaration and say, wait a second, we have got slavery.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说这是一个完美的国家，因为人们立刻就会看到《独立宣言》中“人人生而平等”这句话，然后说，等一下，我们还有奴隶制呢。

sentences.en: This is obviously not true.
sentences.zh: 这显然不是真的。

sentences.en: There are problems here.
sentences.zh: 这里有问题。

sentences.en: But I think people still, even in that critique, they do feel like they're part of something totally unprecedented.
sentences.zh: 但我认为人们仍然觉得，即使在这样的批判中，他们也是某种史无前例的事物的一部分。

sentences.en: And I think the abolition movement in particular really takes this up.
sentences.zh: 我认为废奴运动尤其真正继承了这一点。

sentences.en: Someone like Frederick Douglass, I would point to, is such a critical thinker on this.
sentences.zh: 比如弗雷德里克·道格拉斯，我要指出，他就是这样一个具有批判性思维的人。

sentences.en: Because somebody like Douglass, you know, he himself was born a slave.
sentences.zh: 因为像道格拉斯这样的人，你知道，他自己生来就是奴隶。

sentences.en: He's not confused as to how the country has fallen short.
sentences.zh: 对于国家是如何做得不够好的，他心里跟明镜似的。

sentences.en: And when he even runs away to freedom in the North, he still sees the problem.
sentences.zh: 当他甚至逃往北方的自由之地时，他依然看到了问题所在。

sentences.en: You know, he still faces incredible hostility from white Americans.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他依然面临着来自白人美国人难以想象的敌意。

sentences.en: He gets it.
sentences.zh: 他懂的。

sentences.en: But this project is really falling short of its own founding documents.
sentences.zh: 但这个国家确实辜负了它自己的建国文献。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He looks at the myth and sees it for what it is.
sentences.zh: 他看透了神话的本质。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: To some degree.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上。

sentences.en: But he also believes in this other myth, you could say, that the country is really special and it really needs to live up to being, you know, God's kingdom on earth.
sentences.zh: 但他也相信另一个神话，你可以这么说，那就是这个国家真的很特别，它确实需要不负众望，成为你知道的上帝在人间的国度。

sentences.en: If you imagine, you know, the best society you could ever imagine, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你想象一下，你知道的，你能想象到的最好的社会，对吧？

sentences.en: So for Douglass, this is like full democracy, full equality, all are welcome.
sentences.zh: 所以对道格拉斯来说，这就好比是完全的民主、完全的平等，欢迎所有人。

sentences.en: He's dreaming of a world that isn't here yet.
sentences.zh: 他梦想着一个尚未实现的世界。

sentences.en: He's saying, this is where it's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 他在说，这才是它将要发展到的方向。

sentences.en: So just to give an example, Frederick Douglass has an extraordinary speech that if you read one thing by Frederick Douglass ever,
sentences.zh: 所以举个例子，弗雷德里克·道格拉斯有一篇非凡的演讲，如果你这辈子只读一篇弗雷德里克·道格拉斯的作品，

sentences.en: if you read one thing on July 4th in addition to the Declaration, it's a speech called, What to the Slave is the Fourth of July?
sentences.zh: 如果你在7月4日除了《独立宣言》之外只读一样东西，那就是这篇名为《对于奴隶来说，独立日是什么？》的演讲。

sentences.en: And it's an incredibly beautiful speech.
sentences.zh: 这是一篇极其优美的演讲。

sentences.en: And in it, he basically argues in a very powerful way that the Declaration is really the whole foundation of the country.
sentences.zh: 在其中，他以一种非常有力的方式论证了《独立宣言》确实是整个国家的基石。

sentences.en: Everything in there is almost like a sacred document.
sentences.zh: 里面的一切几乎就像是一份神圣的文献。

sentences.en: And he says, it's the ring bolt to the chain of your nation's destiny.
sentences.zh: 他说，它是维系你国家命运链条上的环扣。

sentences.en: The principles contained in that instrument are saving principles, stand by those principles, be true to them on all occasions, in all places,
sentences.zh: 包含在那份文书中的原则是拯救的原则，坚守这些原则，在所有场合、所有地方都要忠于它们，

sentences.en: against all foes and at whatever coSt.
sentences.zh: 无论面对什么敌人，付出什么代价。

sentences.en: So he's drawing on the Declaration and I think creating kind of a new meaning out of it.
sentences.zh: 所以他在借鉴《独立宣言》，我认为并从中创造出了一种新的含义。

sentences.en: He's saying, these aren't just words that these, you know, slaveholders wrote.
sentences.zh: 他在说，这些不仅仅是你知道的那些蓄奴主义者写下的文字。

sentences.en: They are telling you the roadmap to your destiny as a country.
sentences.zh: 它们在向你们诉说通往你们国家命运的路线图。

sentences.en: And that is quite an inspiring story to tell, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常鼓舞人心的故事。

sentences.en: It is arguably, you know, not strictly the facts of if you went into Jefferson's brain, did he mean to say all that?
sentences.zh: 可以说，这不一定严格符合事实——如果你钻进杰斐逊的脑子里，他真的是那个意思吗？

sentences.en: But it's so powerful.
sentences.zh: 但它是如此强大。

sentences.en: Lincoln takes it up.
sentences.zh: 林肯继承了它。

sentences.en: It's behind the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 它是内战背后的推动力。

sentences.en: It's behind abolition.
sentences.zh: 它是废奴运动背后的推动力。

sentences.en: And so that, to me, is a very clear example of someone taking the Declaration, building a new meaning out of it, and changing his country forever from doing that act.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，这是一个非常清晰的例子：有人采纳了《独立宣言》，从中构建出新的含义，并因这一举动永远改变了他的国家。

sentences.en: At a certain point, and you have already forecast this, the myths come under pretty formal, sustained challenge.
sentences.zh: 在某个特定时刻，正如你已经预料到的那样，这些神话遭到了相当正式、持续的挑战。

sentences.en: When does that start?
sentences.zh: 这从什么时候开始？

sentences.en: I think this is when history itself is changing.
sentences.zh: 我认为正是在历史本身发生变化的时候。

sentences.en: So we've talked about how history used to be seen more as just kind of a literature, right, form of stories.
sentences.zh: 所以我们之前讨论过，过去历史被更多地视为一种文学作品，对吧，一种故事的形式。

sentences.en: But in the late 19th century, you start getting the American Research University.
sentences.zh: 但在19世纪末，你开始迎来美国研究型大学的诞生。

sentences.en: You have universities that are really trying to bring kind of a scientific rigor to all avenues of human knowledge.
sentences.zh: 你有了真正试图将某种科学严谨性引入人类知识各个领域的大学。

sentences.en: And so this is when you get sort of the beginning of professional historians.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是专业历史学家诞生的开端。

sentences.en: And so a historian now is not just a rich guy or a guy with a lot of time on his hands who writes some, you know, pretty compelling stories about his country.
sentences.zh: 因此，现在的历史学家不再只是一个有钱人，或者一个有很多空闲时间、能写出一些关于自己国家的引人入胜的故事的人。

sentences.en: This is a person who is trained as a historian.
sentences.zh: 这是一个受过历史学家专业训练的人。

sentences.en: There's a certain rigor around facts.
sentences.zh: 围绕事实有一种客观的严谨性。

sentences.en: There has to be evidence.
sentences.zh: 必须有证据。

sentences.en: And so once you start doing that, then you're really now in the business of myth-busting.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦你开始这样做，你现在就真正进入了破除神话的行业。

sentences.en: And I think it really begins with, you know, early 20th century, a professor named Charles Beard writes this book.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实始于20世纪初，一个名叫查尔斯·比尔德的教授写了这样一本书。

sentences.en: And he says, OK, these founders, they're not just these altruistic guys who are divinely chosen.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，这些国父们，他们不仅仅是那些被神圣选中的、大公无私的人。

sentences.en: They're people of total virtue.
sentences.zh: 他们并非品格全无瑕疵。

sentences.en: They were actually really elite farmers, aristocrats, who wanted to protect their own material interests.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上是真正的精英地主、贵族，他们想要保护自己的物质利益。

sentences.en: And so that's why they waged revolution.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们发动革命的原因。

sentences.en: Selfless no more.
sentences.zh: 不再无私。

sentences.en: Selfless no more.
sentences.zh: 不再无私。

sentences.en: Completely motivated by self-intereSt.
sentences.zh: 完全是由自私的利益驱动的。

sentences.en: And so once that begins to happen, you really get kind of what feels very familiar to us now, which is the left versus the right.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦这种情况开始发生，你就会真正得到一种对我们来说非常熟悉的东西，那就是左翼对阵右翼。

sentences.en: You've got conservatives saying, whoa, whoa, whoa.
sentences.zh: 你会听到保守派说，等等，等等，等等。

sentences.en: You can't talk like that about the founders.
sentences.zh: 你们不能这样谈论国父们。

sentences.en: You know, you can't talk like that about George Washington, the guy with the cherry tree.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你们不能这样谈论乔治·华盛顿，那个砍了樱桃树的人。

sentences.en: He's not a selfish person.
sentences.zh: 他不是一个自私的人。

sentences.en: He's our model of great national character.
sentences.zh: 他是我们伟大国家品格的典范。

sentences.en: And I think the other side is myth busting.
sentences.zh: 而我认为另一方则在破除神话。

sentences.en: But they're not just saying, oh, my gosh, the whole project is gone.
sentences.zh: 但他们并不是在说，哦天哪，整个事业都完蛋了。

sentences.en: You know, we now learn this about the founders.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们现在才了解到国父们的这一面。

sentences.en: Walk away from the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 对这一切置之不理吧。

sentences.en: They are still trying to find, you know, value and meaning in these stories.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然试图在这些故事中寻找价值和意义。

sentences.en: And so they say, well, OK, they were self-interested.
sentences.zh: 所以他们说，好吧，他们确实有私利。

sentences.en: But that just means that this country has had a problem with elite power.
sentences.zh: 但这只是意味着这个国家一直存在精英权力的问题。

sentences.en: And it hasn't given enough power to sort of the common person.
sentences.zh: 它没有给普通人赋予足够的权力。

sentences.en: And so look at the founding, right?
sentences.zh: 所以看看建国过程，对吧？

sentences.en: The founding shows us why our modern cause is really juSt.
sentences.zh: 建国过程向我们展示了为什么我们现代的事业确实是正义的。

sentences.en: So they're still sort of telling a bigger story about the country and what they want it to be out of the founding.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们仍然在借建国这回事，讲述一个关于这个国家以及他们希望它成为什么样子的宏大故事。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So even the myth busters hang on to some version of the myth.
sentences.zh: 所以即使是那些破除神话的人也保留了某种版本的神话。

sentences.en: Both sides still see value.
sentences.zh: 双方仍然看到了价值。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this dynamic continues for decades.
sentences.zh: 这种动态持续了几十年。

sentences.en: It ebbs and flows.
sentences.zh: 它起伏不定。

sentences.en: There are moments of more agreement.
sentences.zh: 有时会有更多的共识。

sentences.en: There are moments of some disagreement.
sentences.zh: 有时会有一些分歧。

sentences.en: But it really breaks into public view during the bicentennial in 1976.
sentences.zh: 但它真正在公众视野中爆发是在1976年的二百周年国庆期间。

sentences.en: There's a birthday party.
sentences.zh: 有一场生日派对。

sentences.en: And everybody's invited.
sentences.zh: 所有人都在受邀之列。

sentences.en: Like most parties.
sentences.zh: 就像大多数派对一样。

sentences.en: And what's interesting about the bicentennial is that you'll notice there are things that feel very familiar.
sentences.zh: 关于二百周年国庆，有趣的是你会发现有些感觉非常熟悉的事情。

sentences.en: This is a time of a lot of uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 这是一个充满不确定性的时期。

sentences.en: A time of, at this moment, total unrest over the Vietnam War, over race.
sentences.zh: 一个在当时因越南战争和种族问题而彻底动荡的时期。

sentences.en: There's the Watergate scandal.
sentences.zh: 还有水门事件。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This is 1976.
There's a lot going on.
sentences.zh: 有很多事情正在发生。

sentences.en: It's a lot happening.
sentences.zh: 发生了太多事。

sentences.en: This is not a time where people are thinking, this project is going just great.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个人们会觉得“这项事业正进展得非常顺利”的时期。

sentences.en: All of us across the nation are getting into the spirit of 76, 1976, with our own spirit.
sentences.zh: 全国上下所有人都以我们自己的精神融入到76年的精神中，即1976年。

sentences.en: And so the middle of this, the country is trying to somehow mark it.
sentences.zh: 因此，在这个过程中，国家正试图以某种方式来纪念它。

sentences.en: It's 200 years.
sentences.zh: 已经200年了。

sentences.en: You got to do it.
sentences.zh: 你必须这么做。

sentences.en: You can't avoid it.
sentences.zh: 你无法避开它。

sentences.en: Here it is, 1976.
sentences.zh: 就是这样，1976年。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And even in the middle of all this backdrop of absolute domestic unrest, people are still trying to go back to the founding to tell positive stories.
sentences.zh: 甚至在绝对的国内动荡这一背景之下，人们仍然试图回到建国时期去讲述积极的故事。

sentences.en: Even then.
sentences.zh: 即便在那个时候也是如此。

sentences.en: The purpose of our parade is to stand here on the streets and celebrate the birthday of our country as gay people.
sentences.zh: 我们游行的目的，就是作为同性恋者站在这里的街道上，庆祝我们国家的生日。

sentences.en: We make people aware that gay people have always been here in the midst of people before and died for our country.
sentences.zh: 我们让人们意识到，同性恋者一直都在这里，在过去人们中间，甚至为我们的国家牺牲过。

sentences.en: We've been here since the revolution and we will always be here.
sentences.zh: 自革命以来我们就在这里，我们也将永远在这里。

sentences.en: You still see the sharpest critics of the founding myth trying to claim the founding as their own.
sentences.zh: 你仍然可以看到建国神话最激烈的批判者们试图将建国据为己有。

sentences.en: The Afro-American Bicentennial Corporation has been active in any number of substantive projects.
sentences.zh: 美洲黑人二百周年纪念公司积极参与了众多实质性项目。

sentences.en: I think that across the country, we're finding out that blacks, for the most part, look at the Bicentennial in a very different way than...
sentences.zh: 我认为在全国各地，我们发现黑人们在很大程度上看待二百周年国庆的方式与……截然不同

sentences.en: They're trying to invoke it.
sentences.zh: 他们正试图援引它。

sentences.en: They're saying, OK, we are black activists, we're gay activists, and we want to claim the revolutionary spirit.
sentences.zh: 他们在说，好吧，我们是黑人活动家，我们是同性恋活动家，我们想要宣称革命精神。

sentences.en: And it's because of the revolution itself that we think the country can do better.
sentences.zh: 正是因为革命本身，我们认为这个国家可以做得更好。

sentences.en: And so even as they're critiquing the country, they're weaving the founding into their argument and using it to say, this is why you should listen to us.
sentences.zh: 因此，即使他们在批判这个国家，他们也将建国历史编织进他们的论点中，并用它来说明：这就是你们应该听取我们意见的原因。

sentences.en: We are the true inheritors of the founding.
sentences.zh: 我们才是建国事业真正的继承者。

sentences.en: So these fierce debates are unfolding, but even you're saying the biggest critics of the myth are still invoking it and claiming that founding myth as their own,
sentences.zh: 所以这些激烈的辩论正在展开，但即使你这么说，神话的最大批判者们仍然在援引它，并将这个建国神话声称为他们自己的，

sentences.en: but in what now feels more like silos, which doesn't resemble the single unifying force that the mythology was supposed to be.
sentences.zh: 但现在感觉更像是在各自的孤岛中，这已经不像神话原本应该具有的那种单一的凝聚力了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then in the years that followed, the silos just get more and more intense,
sentences.zh: 而在随后的几年里，这些孤岛变得越来越激化，

sentences.en: and it gets harder and harder for everyone to feel like they're having any kind of back-and-forth conversation about the founding.
sentences.zh: 每个人都越来越难以觉得他们还在就建国展开任何形式的来回交流。

sentences.en: And it's harder to imagine, the more you learn, that there is even a way to get back to a single myth anymore.
sentences.zh: 你了解得越多，就越难想象甚至还有什么方法能够回到一个单一的神话。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·罗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth into this, like,
sentences.zh: 甚至早在黑胶唱片时代我在夜店当DJ的时候，你每天晚上都要带300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，你把DJ台变成了这样一个，

sentences.en: living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 充满活力的、由50年前精美老物件组成的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: I'm Wenna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是刘文娜。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我编写了“连线”游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏板块的谜题之一，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，我也喜欢试图捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天都创作“拼字蜜蜂”和“字里行间”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做色听联觉的现象。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 当我听音乐时我能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚刚听到的那些人一样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问nyt.com斜杠games，今天就开始游玩吧。

sentences.en: So, Jalen, talk us through how the silos that we clearly see by 1976, by the bicentennial, bring us to the juncture we are at right now,
sentences.zh: 那么，杰伦，跟我们讲讲，我们在1976年二百周年国庆时分明看到的那些孤岛，是如何把我们带到眼下的这个节点的？

sentences.en: which feels more like a full-on fracturing around the beginning of this country.
sentences.zh: 这个节点感觉更像是围绕这个国家起源的一次全面裂变。

sentences.en: I think through the 70s, you can still see the left and the right fighting over who gets to have the founding.
sentences.zh: 我认为贯穿整个70年代，你仍然可以看到左翼和右翼在争夺谁才有权拥有建国历史。

sentences.en: I think when you get into the Reagan era in the 1980s, it feels like the right is really claiming the higher ground there.
sentences.zh: 我认为当你进入20世纪80年代的里根时代时，感觉右翼在那里真正占据了道德高地。

sentences.en: I think it's time we ask ourselves if we still know the freedoms that were intended for us by the founding fathers.
sentences.zh: 我想是时候该问问自己，我们是否还了解国父们为我们设想的那些自由了。

sentences.en: And they're beginning to really convince more of the country that they are kind of the true inheritors of the founding.
sentences.zh: 他们开始真正说服更多国民，让他们相信自己某种程度上才是建国精神真正的继承者。

sentences.en: Our nation was conceived in liberty, and we have always understood that the fate of our own freedom is tied to the fate of freedom in the world.
sentences.zh: 我们的国家孕育于自由之中，我们始终明白，自身自由的命运与世界自由的命运息息相关。

sentences.en: And so you have, you know, someone like Reagan, this is, you know, really peak Cold War era rhetoric, saying the founding is about personal liberty more than equality.
sentences.zh: 所以你看，像里根这样的人，这可以说是典型的冷战时期激昂陈词，他们认为建国更多是关于个人自由，而不是平等。

sentences.en: If we lose freedom here, there's no place to escape to.
sentences.zh: 如果我们在这里失去了自由，将无处可逃。

sentences.en: This is the last stand on earth.
sentences.zh: 这是地球上的最后坚守。

sentences.en: And this idea that government is beholden to the people, that it has no other source of power except the sovereign people,
sentences.zh: 这种政府效忠于人民、除了主权在民之外没有其他权力来源的理念，

sentences.en: is still the newest and the most unique idea in all the long history of man's relation to man.
sentences.zh: 在人类相互关系的漫长历史中，依然是最崭新、最独特的观念。

sentences.en: And you get the evangelical movement, which is really on the march at this point.
sentences.zh: 而福音派运动也随之兴起，此时正处于蓬勃发展阶段。

sentences.en: This is a nation under God.
sentences.zh: 这是一个受神保佑的国家。

sentences.en: They're saying God has a call on this country.
sentences.zh: 他们声称上帝对这个国家有着呼召。

sentences.en: It was said by our founding fathers, each of the persons who say that mean that here is a nation built upon the Judeo-Christian ethic.
sentences.zh: 国父们曾说过这样的话，每一个说这话的人都意味着这是一个建立在犹太-基督教伦理之上的国家。

sentences.en: And God calls us to be a moral chosen nation, and they are really fusing God and the founding and America into one big thing.
sentences.zh: 而上帝召唤我们成为一个受上帝拣选的道德之国，他们实际上是将上帝、建国和美国融为一体。

sentences.en: The fact that living by God's principles brings a nation to greatness.
sentences.zh: 遵照上帝的原则生活能使一个国家走向伟大。

sentences.en: That and the GOP taking it all in, sort of really pushes this idea of who has the myth, who owns it, who owns the founding, pushes it into sort of a Republican direction.
sentences.zh: 这一点，再加上共和党人的全盘接受，实际上极大地推动了这种观念——谁拥有神话，谁拥有它，谁拥有建国的历史——并将其推向了某种共和党的方向。

sentences.en: And the decades that follow, you know, historians are finding out more and more reasons to be skeptical of mythology about the founding.
sentences.zh: 在随后的几十年里，你知道，历史学家们找到了越来越多的理由去怀疑关于建国的神话。

sentences.en: We are learning a lot more about the lives of the slaves of Jefferson and Washington.
sentences.zh: 我们对杰斐逊和华盛顿奴隶的生活有了更多的了解。

sentences.en: In the late 90s, we get a truly explosive book about Sally Hemings, one of Jefferson's slaves, by the historian Annette Gordon-Reed,
sentences.zh: 在90年代末，历史学家安妮特·戈登-里德出版了一本真正具有轰动效应的书，讲述了杰斐逊的奴隶萨莉·海明斯的故事，

sentences.en: and elevates all these accounts that have been lost that Jefferson, in fact, fathered children with Hemings.
sentences.zh: 并提升了所有那些曾被淹没的记载，即杰斐逊事实上与海明斯育有子女。

sentences.en: And then a year later, there's even DNA testing to prove that she's completely right.
sentences.zh: 而在一年后，甚至有了DNA检测来证明她是完全正确的。

sentences.en: This 200-year-old sex scandal returned to the headlines last week with news of scientific proof now that has confirmed Jefferson's sexual liaison with a woman named Sally Hemings.
sentences.zh: 上周，随着科学证据证实杰斐逊与一个名叫萨莉·海明斯的女子有染，这场延续了200年的性丑闻再次回到了头条新闻中。

sentences.en: And I think the left, seeing all of this, really just sees more reasons for critique, more reasons for skepticism.
sentences.zh: 我想左翼看到这一切，真的只是看到了更多批判的理由，更多怀疑的理由。

sentences.en: How could the same man who wrote about all these great American ideals at the same time quietly be having an affair with someone who was a child?
sentences.zh: 为什么同一个撰写了如此伟大美国理想的人，会同时暗地里与一个未成年人保持私情？

sentences.en: That makes him a liar, fraud, and hypocrite to many people.
sentences.zh: 在许多人看来，这让他成了一个骗子、伪君子和不诚实的人。

sentences.en: And this new information just is really hard for people to absorb.
sentences.zh: 而这些新信息确实让人很难接受。

sentences.en: Jefferson is being depicted variously, as a rapist, a hypocrite, and a dirty old man.
sentences.zh: 杰斐逊被以各种方式描绘成强奸犯、伪君子和一个老色鬼。

sentences.en: If you've grown up thinking about Jefferson as a paragon of American ideals, this is just really tough to swallow.
sentences.zh: 如果你从小把杰斐逊视为美国理想的典范，这确实很难接受。

sentences.en: I would also add to this, there's so much more now about the American Indians.
sentences.zh: 我还要补充一点，现在关于美洲印第安人的内容也多了很多。

sentences.en: The founding fathers were all racists that stole this land from the world.
sentences.zh: 国父们全都是种族主义者，从全世界手中偷走了这片土地。

sentences.en: And sort of what was going on for them during all of this founding and rebellion.
sentences.zh: 以及他们在所有这些建国与叛乱期间究竟经历了什么。

sentences.en: And it's just very hard to integrate a story of absolute dispossession of land with a story of a divinely touched nation, right?
sentences.zh: 要把彻底剥夺土地的历史与一个受神眷顾的国家的历史融合在一起，是非常困难的，对吧？

sentences.en: There are exceptions to this, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，这也有例外。

sentences.en: I'd point to President Obama as someone who has spoken very eloquently about the founding while also acknowledging original sins like slavery.
sentences.zh: 我会指出奥巴马总统就是这样一个人，他既非常雄辩地谈论过建国，同时也承认了诸如蓄奴之类的原罪。

sentences.en: But I think for the most part, you see some elements of the left, I'd say,
sentences.zh: 但我想在很大程度上，你会看到左翼的一些群体，我想说，

sentences.en: really having trouble imagining the founding as a place where you could possibly draw inspiration and hope.
sentences.zh: 他们真的很难把建国想象成一个你能从中汲取灵感和希望的地方。

sentences.en: And so there's just a lot to process that is not merely sort of questioning the myths, but really exploding them.
sentences.zh: 因此，有很多东西需要消化，这不仅仅是对神话的质疑，而是彻底粉碎它们。

sentences.en: And, of course, on its face, there's nothing wrong with the kind of interrogations that the American left is focused on.
sentences.zh: 当然，从表面上看，美国左翼所关注的那种审视并没有什么错。

sentences.en: We are both journalists.
sentences.zh: 我们都是记者。

sentences.en: We are both very invested in the idea of getting to the bottom of the truth.
sentences.zh: 我们都非常投入于探究真相。

sentences.en: And it's often very messy.
sentences.zh: 而且这往往非常繁杂纷乱。

sentences.en: So I wonder what you would say is the downside of this growing fixation on fact-finding.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，你认为这种对事实探寻日益增长的执念，其负面影响是什么？

sentences.en: What's the problem exactly?
sentences.zh: 问题究竟出在哪里？

sentences.en: I am fully in favor of the truth as a journalist, just like you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 作为记者，我和你一样完全支持真相，迈克尔。

sentences.en: And I, in fact, think that to really understand this country and want to fight for its future in some way, the truth is not optional, right?
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为要真正理解这个国家并以某种方式为它的未来而战，真相是不可或缺的，对吧？

sentences.en: But I would also say that that is one bucket of work to be done, the fact-finding, rigorous history.
sentences.zh: 但我也要说，这是需要完成的一类工作，即事实探寻和严谨的历史研究。

sentences.en: There's an entire other area that we've seen in our history, which is not just finding the facts, but finding meaning out of the founding.
sentences.zh: 在我们的历史中，还有另一个完全不同的领域，不仅是寻找事实，更是从建国中寻找意义。

sentences.en: These are not mutually exclusive.
sentences.zh: 这两者并不互相排斥。

sentences.en: You can try to understand the truth of something, but the truth of something and the facts of something don't really tell you what the founding means.
sentences.zh: 你可以试图去理解某事的真相，但某事的真相和事实并不能真正告诉你建国意味着什么。

sentences.en: That's a totally separate avenue of work, you know, in a political argument.
sentences.zh: 在政治争论中，那是完全独立的另一条途径。

sentences.en: And, in fact, sometimes when you get more facts, it can make it harder to do because you're just saying, oh, my gosh, when we look at the history,
sentences.zh: 事实上，有时当你获得更多事实时，反而会使这件事变得更难，因为你会说，天哪，当我们回顾历史时，

sentences.en: it's just one terrible thing after another.
sentences.zh: 简直是一件又一件可怕的事。

sentences.en: It can lead to cynicism, and there are historians who, you know, over time have been very reflective about this and said, what are we doing?
sentences.zh: 这会导致犬儒主义，有些历史学家随着时间的推移对此进行了深刻的反思，并说我们在做什么？

sentences.en: We're trying to reveal facts, but that doesn't mean that we're here to just say we know everything.
sentences.zh: 我们试图揭示事实，但这并不意味着我们在这里只是为了宣称我们无所不知。

sentences.en: We can tell you the meaning of it all.
sentences.zh: 我们能告诉你这一切的意义。

sentences.en: This is just one corner of understanding the American founding, and no amount of facts is going to lead you straight to that answer.
sentences.zh: 这只是理解美国建国的一个角落，再多的事实也无法直接引导你得出那个答案。

sentences.en: I think if I'm reading between the lines of what you're saying, it's that a successful political movement has to find a way to make meaning out of this history.
sentences.zh: 我想如果我能读懂你话中的潜台词，那就是一个成功的政治运动必须找到一种方法，从这段历史中创造意义。

sentences.en: It cannot just articulate flaws.
sentences.zh: 它不能仅仅数落缺点。

sentences.en: And I think it makes sense to bring on stage Make America Great Again as a movement which seeks to call back to the past, to make America great again,
sentences.zh: 我想把“让美国再次伟大”作为一个呼唤回归过去、让美国再次伟大的运动带到台面上是合情合理的，

sentences.en: and which wraps itself in expressions of patriotism and very formally rejects the liberal critique of America throughout its history.
sentences.zh: 它将自己包裹在爱国主义的表达中，并非常明确地拒绝了贯穿美国历史的自由主义批判。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so by now we have a situation where you really feel like, okay, Trump is out there literally hugging and kissing the flag, and we have these 250th celebrations,
sentences.zh: 因此，到目前为止，我们面临这样一种情况：你会真切地感受到，好吧，特朗普在那里 literalmente（字面意思）拥抱亲吻国旗，我们迎来了建国250周年庆典，

sentences.en: and you don't see kind of an organized opposition the way we did in the bicentennial from the left about who owns the history in the first place.
sentences.zh: 而你却没有看到像我们在两百周年时那样，来自左翼的关于究竟谁拥有这段历史的有组织反对声音。

sentences.en: Well, what would it look like to find our way back to a moment when the myths that we're talking about might be more central to our identity as a whole country?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果我们想要找回那个时刻，让咱们刚才谈论的神话重新成为我们整个国家身份认同的核心，这会是什么样子？

sentences.en: And at this point, if for so many people the myth is nothing more than a myth because it's been deconstructed, it's been fact-checked, it's been myth-busted,
sentences.zh: 而在这一点上，如果对许多人来说，神话已经不再是神话，因为它已经被解构、被事实核查、被祛魅，

sentences.en: it would seem pretty hard to get back to that place.
sentences.zh: 想要回到那种状态似乎相当困难。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But what might a middle ground version between fact and myth that is bipartisan, what might that resemble?
sentences.zh: 但是，介于事实与神话之间、能够跨越党派的中间版本，可能会是什么样的呢？

sentences.en: I think it's a place to just begin, and this is what has felt powerful to me, honestly, in the last couple months, is to return again, as I said before,
sentences.zh: 我认为这只是一个起点，老实说，这正是我在过去几个月里感到充满力量的地方，那就是再次回到我之前说过的话，

sentences.en: to the words of Frederick Douglass.
sentences.zh: 回到弗雷德里克·道格拉斯的话中。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think if people can do that, they can sort of access a different strand of the story that I think has gone relatively quiet, which is how people understand the founding,
sentences.zh: 我想如果人们能够做到这一点，他们就能接触到故事的另一条线索，我认这条线索已经变得相对沉寂，那就是人们如何理解建国，

sentences.en: how they make new meaning out of it, how they make their country different with the founding.
sentences.zh: 他们如何从中赋予新的意义，他们如何通过建国让自己的国家变得不同。

sentences.en: And I think once you can see that, you can see that there's kind of, I would argue, almost like a lost tradition of that, right?
sentences.zh: 我想一旦你能看到这一点，你就会发现，我会说，这几乎就像是一个失落的传统，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, how do we get back to a place where we are talking about the founding, discussing the ideals, and not just fighting about what facts should be public or not?
sentences.zh: 比如，我们如何回到这样一个状态：我们在谈论建国，在讨论理想，而不仅仅是在争论哪些事实应该公开，哪些不应该？

sentences.en: And I think the way to get it back is to read these documents.
sentences.zh: 我认为找回它的方法就是去阅读这些文献。

sentences.en: Let's read the Declaration.
sentences.zh: 让我们来读读《独立宣言》。

sentences.en: Just that opening part.
sentences.zh: 就读开头那部分。

sentences.en: We don't need to get into all the ways, all the grievances of the colonists, necessarily.
sentences.zh: 我们不一定非要深入探讨殖民地居民的种种方式和所有的苦情。

sentences.en: Let's just read that opening lines.
sentences.zh: 让我们就读读那些开篇之句。

sentences.en: Let's read the Gettysburg Address.
sentences.zh: 让我们读读《葛底斯堡演说》。

sentences.en: These are not long documents to read, but I think, for me, when I reread them, it just got my imagination going of like, oh, there's so many possibilities.
sentences.zh: 这些都不是长篇大论，但对我和来说，当我重新阅读它们时，我的想象力就被激发了，心想，哦，这里有这么多的可能性。

sentences.en: There's so many ways to interpret the founding.
sentences.zh: 有这么多的方式来解读建国。

sentences.en: And that's where we need to sort of be thinking.
sentences.zh: 这才是我们需要思考的方向。

sentences.en: And if we can have that conversation, you know, in a way, we'll never agree on what liberty means.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能展开那样的对话，你知道，在某种程度上，我们永远无法就“自由”的含义达成一致。

sentences.en: How could you possibly, like, that's just the biggest possible idea.
sentences.zh: 你怎么可能做到呢，这简直是最大可能的概念了。

sentences.en: It's hard to agree on what equality means.
sentences.zh: 很难就“平等”的含义达成一致。

sentences.en: But I think the country has kind of found its bearings again when people are really engaged in debates and conversations about that.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，当人们真正参与到关于这些的辩论和对话中时，这个国家算是重新找回了方向。

sentences.en: Well, Jalen, I wanted to finish, if you'll let me, by asking you a more personal question.
sentences.zh: 好的，杰伦，如果你允许的话，我想问你一个更私人的问题来作为结束。

sentences.en: Because you are the child of immigrants.
sentences.zh: 因为你是移民的孩子。

sentences.en: I know this because you wrote an entire book about the history of immigration in America, and you talk about your family's experience.
sentences.zh: 我知道这一点，因为你写过一整本关于美国移民历史的书，你在书中谈到了你家庭的经历。

sentences.en: And I wonder what all these questions about the American founding myth meant to your family, especially your parents, as they settled into the United States.
sentences.zh: 我想知道关于美国建国神话的这些问题，对于你的家庭，尤其是你的父母在美利坚安顿下来时意味着什么。

sentences.en: I think for my family, the element of this that's so powerful is that it feels like a country that, for better and for worse, is really swept up in ideals,
sentences.zh: 我想对我的家庭而言，其中最具力量的元素是，它感觉这是一个无论好坏、真正深陷于理想之中的国家，

sentences.en: in trying to make something better.
sentences.zh: 一个试图让事物变得更好的国家。

sentences.en: I think about my dad, who loves reading Lincoln's writing, he loves to read it.
sentences.zh: 我想到了我的父亲，他热爱阅读林肯的著作，他非常喜欢读。

sentences.en: Because he's reading about a person who is just, you know, in the darkest hour of our country, when the whole thing feels like it's going to be loSt.
sentences.zh: 因为他在阅读一个这样的人：他在我们国家最黑暗的时刻，当一切似乎都注定要失败时，

sentences.en: There's someone who still believes that the country can be something that has not been before, and that has never been seen before.
sentences.zh: 依然有人相信这个国家可以成为一个前所未有、闻所未闻的存在。

sentences.en: And so, I think if you want to join in that, that's why I think, not for, I won't speak for all immigrants, I wouldn't nearly,
sentences.zh: 所以，我想如果你想加入其中，这就是为什么我认为——我不会代表所有移民，我绝不会这样做——

sentences.en: but I think there are some immigrants who just are the deepest believers in America, in its myths.
sentences.zh: 但我认为有些移民恰恰是对美国、对它的神话最坚定的信仰者。

sentences.en: And there are reasons to be cynical, there are reasons every day to be disillusioned.
sentences.zh: 这里有玩世不恭的理由，每天都有感到幻灭的理由。

sentences.en: But it's also a place that's always imagining something else, right?
sentences.zh: 但这也是一个总是在想象别的东西的地方，对吧？

sentences.en: That's how it begins.
sentences.zh: 一切就是这样开始的。

sentences.en: It begins by imagining a different kind of democracy that's never been seen before.
sentences.zh: 它始于对一种前所未见的、不同民主形态的想象。

sentences.en: And it just keeps reimagining it into something.
sentences.zh: 并且它不断地将其重新想象成某种形态。

sentences.en: And I think that just, to me, like provokes dreaming and hoping, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为这对我来说，能激发出梦想和希望，对吧？

sentences.en: It's like, what could this be?
sentences.zh: 就像是，这会变成什么样？

sentences.en: Like, let's see.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看。

sentences.en: Let's try.
sentences.zh: 让我们试试。

sentences.en: And I think the challenge for us is to figure out, just as other people have done before, what does all of it mean to us today?
sentences.zh: 我认为对我们来说，挑战在于去弄清楚，就像以前其他人所做的那样，这一切对今天的我们意味着什么？

sentences.en: What are the ideals?
sentences.zh: 理想是什么？

sentences.en: How do we match up now?
sentences.zh: 我们现在该如何衡量？

sentences.en: And what does that mean for what we want to do next?
sentences.zh: 这对我们接下来想做的事情意味着什么？

sentences.en: We're never going to agree on all of it, but is there a way to even get anywhere closer to something like a unified conversation about it?
sentences.zh: 我们永远无法在所有事情上达成一致，但有没有办法让我们哪怕稍微接近一下关于它的某种统一对话？

sentences.en: And I have to think that the founding is still the beginning.
sentences.zh: 我不得不认为建国仍然是一个起点。

sentences.en: And what better place to begin to try to find some story that holds us together again?
sentences.zh: 还有什么地方比这里更适合作为起点，去寻找一个能将我们重新凝聚在一起的故事呢？

sentences.en: Well, Jalen, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，杰伦，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: The Russian military bombarded Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, with waves of ballistic missiles and drones, in an act of retaliation for weeks of Ukrainian attacks deep inside of Russia.
sentences.zh: 作为对乌克兰数周前深入俄罗斯腹地袭击的报复，俄军用一波又一波的弹道导弹和无人机轰炸了乌克兰首都基辅。

sentences.en: Those attacks on Russia have caused widespread fuel shortages across the country and put enormous pressure on President Vladimir Putin,
sentences.zh: 这些针对俄罗斯的袭击导致全国范围内燃料严重短缺，并给弗拉基米尔·普京总统带来了巨大压力，

sentences.en: who began the war with Ukraine four years ago.
sentences.zh: 他在四年前发起了对乌克兰的战争。

sentences.en: Ukrainian officials said that Russia's retaliatory attacks killed at least 21 people and injured at least 85 more.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰官员表示，俄罗斯的报复性袭击造成至少21人死亡，至少85人受伤。

sentences.en: These are extremely dangerous conditions, and they will affect every part of our city.
sentences.zh: 这些是极其危险的状况，它们将影响我们城市的每一个角落。

sentences.en: Dangerous heat blanketed tens of millions of Americans on Thursday as high temperatures that began in the Midwest moved to the East Coast,
sentences.zh: 周四，危险的高温笼罩了数千万美国人，随着从美国中西部开始的高温天气向东海岸移动，

sentences.en: hovering around 100 degrees from Atlanta to New York City, where Mayor Zoran Mandani warned residents to avoid the outdoors.
sentences.zh: 从亚特兰大到纽约市，气温徘徊在华氏100度（约38摄氏度）左右，纽约市长佐兰·曼达尼警告居民避免外出。

sentences.en: The single most important thing you can do in these temperatures is to stay indoors with air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 在这种气温下你能做的最重要的一件事就是待在有空调的室内。

sentences.en: If you can't avoid going outside during the hottest hours of the day, please do so.
sentences.zh: 如果你在一天中最热的几小时无法避免外出，请务必注意。

sentences.en: Forecasters blamed the high temperatures on a heat dome in which a sprawling high-pressure weather system is pushing warm air toward the ground.
sentences.zh: 气象预报员将高温归咎于热穹顶效应，一个庞大的高压天气系统正在将暖空气推向地面。
